Posted February 1, 2006
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
An Update from Michele Kubby. Will Marinol Work? An Arraignment Hearing In Auburn at 1PM on Tuesday, January 31st.

Yesterday was not a good day for justice, but it was a great day for fans of rampant stupidity. I have written about Placer County law enforcement many times in the past, but today was truly over the top. At least there was a large media presence to witness the absurdity of it all.
See
 Placer County, Still Murderous After All These Years. Kubbys Find Secret Death Warrant Signed by Disqualified Judge. Key To Canadian Refuge, If Not Justice In California.

After being locked up since he returned to DEAland, and having never been seen by a doctor, Steve Kubby was brought in handcuffs and an orange jailhouse jump suit into the jail court at the end of a long parade of sad looking young men and middle-aged women.

All of the other prisoners were handcuffed together, but Steve was by himself, just as he is kept in solitary confinement. He smiled as he saw that the room was full of his friends and supporters, including Steve Tuck who was sitting in the front row. (Of course, Tuck had just medicated on the jailhouse steps, as a dozen or so of the local constabulary glowered impotently.)
See
Steve Tuck Is A Free Man. Vindicated. Recuperating from Five Year Ordeal. Will Return to Mining Business in Canada After First Of Year.

Bill McPike, Kubbys attorney, was with him for about 45 minutes this morning and told the assemble throng of reporters that Steve is not doing well, but still had not been seen by a doctor. He also said that he (McPike) had talked with the DA, Fennochio, who said he was leaving the case in the hands of the Assistant DA, Chris Cattran. (Presumably, he wants to be able preserve plausible deniability. It wont work.)

It would seem that there is at least the possibility of a deal that would give Kubby house arrest while he appeals his conviction, but that is very uncertain. He might be locked up for about 90 days for the balance of his probated sentence.

Steve is now being given Marinol, and that seems to help him some, but it is almost certain that it will not be enough to control his symptoms, much less retard the progression of his adrenal cancer. His life remains in great danger, and right now he is the subject (victim) of a bizarre medical experiment that should outrage the medical profession. (Quack, quack.)

He is also as much a victim of torture as anyone in Guantanamo or Abu Ghraib. Of course, if he were an accused terrorist, Amnesty International would have been there today.

As things stand now, Steve may still face up to three years for the supposed felony convictions for the possession of minute amounts of psychedelics, which the police extracted from plant material supposedly found in a film canister in the Kubbys guestroom.

After the hearings, Cattran tried to pretend that this was just another case, and everything is being handled routinely. However, when journalist Pat McCartney asked him about why the conversion of Steves conviction from a misdemeanor to a felony had been handled by judges who had been recused from the case, Cattran refused to answer and stormed away. Not a cool way to impress visiting media.

Before his hasty exit, I was able to ask him if he had been contacted by anyone from Immigration Canada, and he actually looked surprised. He said that he had not heard from them at all. He also acknowledged that he had told the media that Kubby would be arrested  as a matter of course  when he was forcibly renditioned to DEAland.
See
Steve Kubbys Life Is In Danger Because Immigration Canada and California Law Enforcement Broke the Law.

Of course, this more proof that Immigration Canada has lied through out the Kubby and Tuck refugee hearings. But why?

Do the people of Canada want to face the truth about what is being done in their names? Certainly the American people should have been able to see for themselves the surreal scene in that courtroom. Look in the mirror, America! See what you have become!

And look in the mirror, dear reader. What have you done for freedom today?

I will be back in Auburn on Friday morning, but in the meantime, we must continue to demand that Kubby either be released at once or be given proper medical care, including whole cannabis. California should contact Attorney General Lockyer and demand an investigation of Placer Countys handling of the Kubby case from the beginning. If  God forbid  Steve dies, there will be no escaping an investigation. It would be much better to free Steve and do it now and not have to add judicial/prosecutorial murder to the list of surreal injustices in this case.
See
Steve Kubby Is the Only One In This Story Who Has NOT Broken The Law, But He Faces the Death Penalty.
